senses.def: a lawyer who works for the government and tries to prove in court that someone is guilty of a crime
examples: The prosecutor argued that the defendant had planned the robbery for weeks.
Federal prosecutors dropped the charges after new evidence emerged.

note: In the US, a local prosecutor is usually called a "district attorney" (DA). The opposite side is the "defense attorney".

senses.def: the chance or possibility that something will happen, especially something good
examples: There is little prospect of an agreement before the deadline.
The prospect of moving abroad both excited and scared her.

senses.def: chances of success in the future, especially in a career (usually plural)
examples: A degree in engineering will improve your job prospects.
The team's prospects for the playoffs look bright this season.

senses.def: likely or expected to become something or to do something in the future
examples: The college offers campus tours for prospective students and their parents.
We showed the apartment to three prospective buyers this weekend.

senses.def: the state of being successful and having plenty of money
examples: The postwar years brought a period of economic prosperity.
Trade with its neighbors is key to the region's long-term prosperity.

senses.def: to keep someone or something safe from harm, damage, or loss
examples: Wear sunscreen to protect your skin from the sun.
The new law is designed to protect workers from unfair dismissal.

note: Use "protect from" or "protect against", not "protect of".

senses.def: the act of keeping someone or something safe, or the state of being kept safe
examples: The vaccine gives protection against several strains of flu.
Witnesses in the case were placed under police protection.

senses.def: designed to keep someone or something safe from harm
examples: Workers must wear protective gear when handling chemicals.
The phone comes with a protective case.

senses.def: wanting to keep someone you love safe, sometimes too much
examples: He's very protective of his younger sister.
Some parents become overly protective once their kids start dating.

note: Pattern: be protective OF someone (not "to").

senses.def: a natural substance in foods like meat, eggs, and beans that the body needs to grow and repair itself
examples: Lentils are a cheap source of protein for vegetarians.
Athletes often drink protein shakes after a workout.

senses.def: a public action or statement showing strong disagreement with something
examples: Thousands of students joined the protest outside city hall.
The fans left the stadium early in protest at the ticket prices.

senses.tr: protesto etmek, itiraz etmek, karşı çıkmak
senses.def: to say or show publicly that you strongly disagree with something
examples: Residents protested against the plan to close the local hospital.
Nurses marched downtown to protest low pay.

note: Stress: noun PRO-test, verb usually pro-TEST. In American English the verb can take a direct object: "protest the war".

senses.def: a person who takes part in a public protest
examples: Police used tear gas to break up a crowd of protesters.
Protesters held signs demanding action on climate change.

note: Also spelled "protestor".

senses.def: the official rules about correct behavior on formal or diplomatic occasions
examples: According to protocol, the president greets foreign leaders at the airport.
He broke royal protocol by hugging the queen.

senses.def: a set of rules or procedures to follow in a particular situation, e.g. in medicine or computing
examples: Hospitals updated their safety protocols during the outbreak.
The two computers communicate using a secure protocol.

senses.tr: gururlu, (biriyle/bir şeyle) gurur duyan, iftihar eden
senses.def: feeling pleased about something you have done or about someone connected to you
examples: We're so proud of you for finishing the marathon.
She was proud to represent her country at the Olympics.

senses.def: having too high an opinion of yourself, or too much self-respect to ask for help
examples: He was too proud to admit he needed money from his parents.

note: Use "proud of", not "proud with". Noun: pride ("take pride in").

senses.def: to use facts or evidence to show that something is true
examples: Lawyers could not prove that he was at the scene of the crime.
Scientists have proved that the drug reduces the risk of stroke.

senses.def: to turn out to be a particular thing, as shown by what happens over time
examples: The new software proved to be more difficult than expected.
Finding a parking space downtown proved impossible.

note: Past participle: proved or proven; "proven" is common in American English, especially as an adjective ("a proven method").

senses.def: to give something to someone or make it available for them to use
examples: The hotel provides free breakfast for all guests.
Can you provide more details about the incident?

senses.def: to give someone the money, food, and things they need to live (provide for)
examples: He works two jobs to provide for his family.

note: Patterns: provide someone WITH something, or provide something FOR/TO someone. Not "provide someone something".

senses.def: one of the main areas some countries are divided into, with its own local government
examples: Quebec is the largest province in Canada.
Heavy flooding hit several southern provinces last week.

senses.def: the parts of a country outside the capital or main cities (the provinces)
examples: The theater company tours the provinces every summer.

note: Turkey's 81 "iller" are usually called provinces in English.

senses.def: relating to a province or its local government
examples: The provincial government announced new funding for schools.
Provincial elections will be held next spring.

senses.def: outside the capital, or having old-fashioned, narrow-minded attitudes (often disapproving)
examples: She found the town's attitudes provincial after years in New York.

senses.def: the act of supplying something that people need
examples: The city is responsible for the provision of clean water.
There is very little provision for disabled travelers at the station.

senses.def: a condition or rule in a law or legal agreement
examples: A provision in the contract allows either side to cancel with 30 days' notice.

senses.def: supplies of food and other necessary things, especially for a journey (provisions)
examples: The hikers packed enough provisions for a week in the mountains.

senses.tr: (tepki, tartışma) yol açmak, neden olmak, uyandırmak
senses.def: to cause a particular reaction or feeling, especially a negative one
examples: The decision to raise taxes provoked an angry response from voters.
Her speech provoked a heated debate online.

senses.def: to deliberately make someone angry so that they react
examples: Don't let him provoke you into a fight.

senses.def: relating to the treatment of mental illness
examples: He spent two months in a psychiatric hospital after the breakdown.
The prisoner was given a psychiatric evaluation before trial.

note: The "p" is silent: /saɪ-/. A psychiatrist is a medical doctor; a psychologist usually is not.

senses.def: connected with the mind and the way it affects feelings and behavior
examples: Long periods of isolation can cause serious psychological harm.
Losing in the final minute was a big psychological blow to the team.

senses.def: a person trained in psychology, who studies the mind or helps people with emotional problems
examples: The school hired a psychologist to support students after the tragedy.
Child psychologists say routines help young kids feel safe.

senses.def: the scientific study of the mind and how it affects behavior
examples: She majored in psychology at a state university.
The course covers the basics of child psychology.

senses.def: the way a particular person or group thinks and behaves
examples: Marketers study the psychology of shoppers to boost sales.

senses.def: a place where people go to drink alcohol and other drinks, and often eat, especially in Britain
examples: After the game, we went to an Irish pub downtown.
The pub serves fish and chips and local beer.

note: "Pub" is a typically British word. Americans usually say "bar", though "pub" is used for British or Irish-style bars.

senses.def: for or relating to people in general, or provided by the government for everyone
examples: Smoking is banned in all public places.
Public opinion has turned against the war.

senses.def: ordinary people in general (the public)
examples: The museum is open to the public on weekends.
The government failed to warn the public about the risks.

note: In the US, a "public school" is free and government-funded; in Britain it is an expensive private school.

senses.def: the act of printing a book, article, etc. and making it available to the public
examples: The novel became a bestseller within a month of its publication.
The study was submitted for publication in a medical journal.

senses.def: a book, magazine, newspaper, or similar thing that has been published
examples: The magazine is one of the most respected publications in the industry.

senses.def: attention given to someone or something by the media, or the business of attracting that attention
examples: The scandal brought a lot of unwanted publicity to the company.
The band did a publicity tour before the album came out.

note: "There's no such thing as bad publicity" is a common saying.

senses.def: to print and sell a book, magazine, etc., or to make something available online
examples: Her first novel was published when she was only 22.
The company publishes children's books in twelve languages.

senses.def: to make information officially available to the public
examples: The researchers published their findings in a leading journal.
The government will publish the report next month.

senses.def: the business of preparing and selling books, magazines, etc.
examples: She has worked in publishing for over twenty years.
Digital publishing has changed how authors reach readers.

senses.def: to hold something and move it toward you or behind you
examples: Pull the door hard; it sticks in cold weather.
Two horses pulled the cart up the hill.

senses.def: to move a vehicle somewhere (pull over, pull into, pull out)
examples: A police officer pulled me over for speeding.
The train pulled into the station ten minutes late.

senses.def: an act of pulling, or a strong force that attracts
examples: Give the rope a good pull.
The pull of city life was too strong for her to stay in the village.

note: Many phrasal verbs: pull off (succeed), pull through (survive), pull out (withdraw). Opposite: push.

senses.def: the regular beat of your heart, which you can feel at your wrist or neck
examples: The nurse took my pulse and blood pressure.
Her pulse raced as she waited for the results.

senses.def: the dried seeds of plants like lentils, beans, and peas, eaten as food (pulses)
examples: Pulses such as chickpeas and lentils are rich in fiber.

collocations: keep a finger on the pulse
note: "Have your finger on the pulse" means to know the latest developments in a field.

senses.def: a machine that pushes liquid, gas, or air into or out of something
examples: I need a bike pump; my back tire is flat.
The water pump in the basement broke during the storm.

senses.def: to move liquid, gas, or air somewhere using a pump or a similar action
examples: The heart pumps blood around the body.
Firefighters pumped water out of the flooded tunnel.

senses.def: to put a lot of money into something
examples: Investors have pumped billions into electric car startups.

note: Informal "pumped (up)" means very excited. A "gas pump" is a fuel pump at a gas station.

senses.def: to hit someone or something hard with a closed hand
examples: He punched the wall in frustration and broke his hand.
The boxer was punched in the face in the first round.

senses.def: a hard hit with a closed hand
examples: She threw a punch at the man who grabbed her bag.
The final punch knocked him out.

senses.def: a drink made by mixing fruit juices, often with alcohol
examples: There was a big bowl of fruit punch at the party.

note: "Pack a punch" means to have a strong effect. "Punch line" is the funny last part of a joke.

senses.def: to make someone suffer because they have broken a rule or the law
examples: The boy was punished for lying to his teachers.
Companies that pollute rivers should be severely punished.

senses.def: something done to someone because they have done something wrong
examples: As punishment, she lost her phone for a week.
The judge said the punishment should fit the crime.

note: "Capital punishment" means the death penalty.

senses.def: a loud, fast, aggressive type of rock music that became popular in the late 1970s
examples: He grew up listening to punk and played guitar in a garage band.
The club hosts punk and metal shows on Fridays.

senses.def: a fan of punk music; also (informal, American) a young person who behaves badly
examples: Some punk spray-painted the side of our garage.

note: In informal American English, calling someone "a punk" is an insult meaning a troublemaker.

senses.def: a child or young person who goes to school, or someone taught by a particular teacher
examples: The school has about 300 pupils between ages five and eleven.
The old piano teacher still remembers her favorite pupil.

senses.def: the small black circle in the middle of your eye
examples: Your pupils get bigger in the dark to let in more light.

note: "Pupil" (school child) sounds British or formal; Americans usually say "student" at all levels.

senses.def: to buy something (more formal than "buy")
examples: Tickets can be purchased online or at the box office.
The city purchased the land to build a new park.

senses.def: the act of buying something, or something that you have bought
examples: Keep your receipt as proof of purchase.
A house is the biggest purchase most people ever make.

note: Pronounced /ˈpɜːrtʃəs/, not "pur-chase" with -chase. More formal than "buy".

senses.def: not mixed with anything else
examples: The sweater is made of pure wool.
This juice is 100 percent pure orange with no added sugar.

senses.def: clean and free from harmful substances
examples: The mountain air was cold and pure.

senses.def: used for emphasis, meaning complete or nothing but
examples: We met by pure chance at an airport in Chicago.
Her face showed pure joy when she saw the puppy.

senses.def: only, completely, and for no other reason
examples: I took the job purely for the money.
The decision was made on purely financial grounds.

senses.def: having the color you get by mixing red and blue
examples: She wore a purple dress to the wedding.
His face turned purple with anger.

senses.def: the color made by mixing red and blue
examples: Purple was once a color worn only by kings and emperors.

senses.def: the reason something is done or made, or what it is meant to achieve
examples: What is the purpose of your visit to the United States?
The meeting's main purpose was to discuss the budget.

senses.def: a feeling of having an aim that makes life feel meaningful
examples: Volunteering gave him a new sense of purpose after he retired.

note: "On purpose" means deliberately: "He broke it on purpose." Not "with purpose".

senses.def: to try to achieve something or continue doing an activity over a long period
examples: After college, she moved to Los Angeles to pursue a career in acting.
The police decided not to pursue the case any further.

senses.def: to follow or chase someone in order to catch them
examples: Officers pursued the stolen car for several miles.

senses.def: the act of trying to get or achieve something
examples: The Declaration of Independence mentions life, liberty, and the pursuit of happiness.
He left home in pursuit of a better life.

senses.def: the act of chasing someone
examples: The suspect crashed his car during a high-speed police pursuit.

senses.def: an activity you spend time doing, especially for pleasure
examples: Hiking and fishing are popular outdoor pursuits in the area.

senses.def: to use your hands or body to move something away from you, or to press a button
examples: Can you help me push the car off the road?
Push the green button to start the machine.

senses.def: to try hard to make someone do something or to make something happen
examples: Her parents pushed her to study medicine.
Activists are pushing for stricter gun laws.

senses.def: an act of pushing, or a strong effort to achieve something
examples: Give the door a push; it isn't locked.
The company is making a big push into the Asian market.

note: "Pushy" means too forceful in getting what you want. A "pushover" is someone easy to persuade.

senses.def: to move something into a particular place or position
examples: Put your keys on the table so you don't lose them.
She put the baby to bed at eight.

senses.def: to cause someone or something to be in a particular state or situation
examples: The scandal put the mayor in a very difficult position.
Rising costs have put many small shops out of business.

senses.def: to say or express something in a particular way
examples: To put it simply, we can't afford a new car right now.

note: Irregular: put – put – put. Many phrasal verbs: put off (postpone), put up with (tolerate), put out (extinguish).

senses.def: a game or toy that you have to think carefully about to solve or put together
examples: My grandfather does the crossword puzzle every morning.
The kids spent the afternoon putting together a 500-piece puzzle.

senses.def: something that is difficult to understand or explain
examples: How the thieves got into the vault remains a puzzle.

senses.def: to make someone confused because they cannot understand something
examples: His sudden resignation puzzled everyone in the office.

senses.def: a skill, quality, or experience that makes you suitable for a job
examples: The main qualification for the job is five years of sales experience.
He lacks the qualifications to run a large hospital.

senses.def: an exam you have passed or a course you have completed
examples: She left school without any formal qualifications.

senses.def: the fact of reaching a later stage of a competition
examples: The win secured the team's qualification for the World Cup.

note: "Qualifications" for degrees and certificates is more British; Americans often say "credentials".

senses.def: having the training, exams, or experience needed for a particular job
examples: Only qualified electricians should work on the wiring.
She's highly qualified for the position.

senses.def: limited in some way; not complete
examples: The plan received qualified support from the board.

senses.def: to complete the training or exams needed to do a particular job
examples: He qualified as a nurse after three years of training.

senses.def: to have the right to do or receive something because you meet certain conditions
examples: Families with low incomes qualify for free school lunches.
She qualified for the final with the second-fastest time.

senses.def: relating to how good something is or what it is like, rather than how much of it there is
examples: The researchers combined survey data with qualitative interviews.
There is a qualitative difference between the two teaching methods.

note: Academic word. Opposite: quantitative (based on numbers and amounts).
